title: Probe priming, hot-swap, and cost-aware scheduler playbook
author: Marina Kwon
content:
Overview
========
This playbook describes a repeatable lifecycle for probe priming, live hot-swap of probe sets, and a cost-aware scheduler used to allocate evaluation budget across shadow and canary cohorts. It is intended for evaluation engineers, SREs who operate evaluator fleets, and model-onboarding teams coordinating quantization rollouts. The procedures balance fidelity, cost, and tenant isolation while enabling rapid response to regressions caused by quant or cache changes.

Why this exists
---------------
- Probe priming reduces noise when moving between model variants and quant levels by ensuring warm seeds and anchor examples are present before measuring drift.
- Hot-swap of probe sets enables fast replacement of flaky or high-cost probes without full evaluator redeploys.
- The scheduler enforces a cost budget and allocates probes across cohorts (shadow, canary, production-sampled) according to policy and SLO constraints.

Scope and non-goals
------------------
Scope:
- Shadow and canary evaluation within Redwood-hosted evaluator fleet and private evaluator sidecars.
- Interaction with quant shadow cohorts and KV-cache–sensitive workloads.

Non-goals:
- Full annotation workflows (use annotator playbooks).
- External third-party evaluator federation protocols (covered in evaluator-interchange-format docs).

Roles and ownership
-------------------
- Owner: Applied ML Evaluations team (primary contact: Marina Kwon).
- Fleet SRE: implements and operates the scheduler service (alerts, scaling).
- Onboarding PM: approves budget window, target cohorts.
- Incident runbook owner: Eng SRE on-call.

High-level workflow
-------------------
1. Define probe seed set and priming criteria in the Probe Manifest. Include anchor examples, per-probe cost estimate, and sensitivity metadata.
2. Reserve evaluation budget for the rollout window (daily token cap for shadow).
3. Run priming stage: synthetic warmups + anchor replay to populate KV caches and warm model weights.
4. Start soft canary with low traffic and scheduler-enforced budget.
5. If metrics pass thresholds, increase traffic; if not, hot-swap probes and/or rollback per rollback policy.

Probe Manifest schema (text table)
--------------------------------
| field | description | example | required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| probe_id | unique id for asset | anchor-en-us-001 | yes |
| category | semantic slice label | payment-instruction | yes |
| estimated_tokens | average tokens per probe | 42 | yes |
| cost_weight | relative cost multiplier for scheduler | 1.2 | yes |
| priming_hits | number of anchor replays recommended | 10 | no |
| sensitivity_tags | tags indicating quant/cache sensitivity | kv-cache-sensitive, low-temp | no |

Scheduler policy and rules
--------------------------
- Inputs: daily_token_budget, max_cost_per_probe, cohort_weights (shadow:canary:prod-sample), probe_priority_score (computed).
- Probe priority score = base_priority * sensitivity_multiplier / sqrt(estimated_tokens) where sensitivity_multiplier is 2.0 for kv-cache-sensitive probes.
- Scheduler enforces: total_estimated_daily_tokens <= daily_token_budget; never schedule > cohort_max_concurrency per tenant.
- Backoff rule: if a probe causes > 3% spike in latency tail or > 2x token cost deviance, throttle that probe and mark for hot-swap.

Configuration examples
----------------------
YAML example for an evaluator job (annotated):

scheduler:
  daily_token_budget: 5_000_000
  cohort_weights:
    shadow: 0.5
    canary: 0.2
    prod_sample: 0.3
  max_cost_per_probe_usd: 0.12
  hot_swap_thresholds:
    latency_tail_p99_pct_increase: 3.0
    token_cost_variance_multiplier: 2.0

probe_manifest:
  - probe_id: anchor-en-us-001
    category: payment-instruction
    estimated_tokens: 42
    cost_weight: 1.2
    priming_hits: 8
    sensitivity_tags: [kv-cache-sensitive, functioncall]

Priming procedure (step-by-step)
--------------------------------
1. Reserve a priming window of 30m to 2h depending on model cold-start characteristics.
2. Deploy priming runner: replay anchor probes with decreasing temperature and incremental context lengths.
3. Verify warmup metrics: KV hit-rate > 90%, model initialization latency < baseline * 1.1, no OOMs.
4. Snapshot primed state if running in private evaluator sidecars (artifact id).
5. Signal readiness to the scheduler to begin live canary.

Hot-swap procedure (fast replacement)
------------------------------------
1. Detection: scheduler flags probe as degraded (based on telemetry contract).
2. Quarantine: reduce probe sampling weight to 0 and move to quarantined bucket.
3. Replace: pick next candidate probe from replacement pool (match on category and tokens).
4. Priming: run quick priming mini-run (priming_hits=2) for the replacement.
5. Resume: restore normal sampling weight and monitor for stabilization window (default 60 minutes).
6. Postmortem: tag original probe with failure reason, cost delta, and owner for triage.

Telemetry contract (required signals)
-----------------------------------
- per-probe: probe_id, timestamp, probe_latency_p50/p90/p99_ms, tokens_consumed, model_version, quant_profile, kv_cache_hit_rate, cohort, tenant_id (if applicable), error_class.
- per-job: total_tokens_consumed, total_cost_usd_estimate, scheduled_probe_count, priming_status, scheduler_decisions (reason for skip/hot-swap).

SLOs and alert thresholds
-------------------------
- Scheduler correctness: 99.9% decisions executed within 5s of decision time.
- Priming success rate: target 95% of priming runs meet warm-up KPIs (kv hit-rate, latency).
- Hot-swap detection precision: > 90% of flagged probes correspond to measurable cost or quality regressions on follow-up.
- Alerts: page SRE on any priming run OOM or >5% error_rate during canary.

Cost accounting and attribution
------------------------------
- Per-probe cost = estimated_tokens * region_token_price * cost_weight.
- The scheduler writes daily ledger entries to the Eval Ledger service with tags: probe_id, model_version, quant_profile, tenant_id.
- Chargebacks: Owned teams are charged internal evaluation credits for shadow runs exceeding allocated budget windows.

Acceptance and rollout checklist
-------------------------------
- [ ] Probe Manifest reviewed and signed by Onboarding PM.
- [ ] Daily token budget approved by Finance for the rollout window.
- [ ] Scheduler policy set and dry-run simulated for 48h.
- [ ] Priming run passes warm-up KPIs.
- [ ] Canary run at 1% traffic for 6h with no regressions.
- [ ] Increase to target traffic split over 24h.

Rollback and mitigation ladders
------------------------------
Immediate rollback triggers:
1. Delta fidelity regression > threshold (slice-anchored metrics).
2. Token cost exceedance > 2x forecast for three consecutive intervals.
3. Sustained latency tail increase > 5% at p99 for 30 minutes.

Mitigation steps (fast path):
1. Pause canary and reduce cohort weights by 80%.
2. Hot-swap to alternative probe set or previous model artifact.
3. If caused by quant profile, fallback to higher-precision variant and notify model-onboarding.

Post-incident triage items to capture
-----------------------------------
- root cause hypothesis (code, quant, data, scheduling mistake)
- timeline of scheduler decisions and probe events
- cost impact and tokens burned outside budget
- recommended changes to probe manifest or scheduler heuristics

Example CLI snippets
--------------------
# Trigger a priming run for a manifest artifact
redwood-evalctl priming start --manifest-id anchor-manifest-202611 --window 45m --region us-west-2

# Query scheduled decisions in the last 24h
redwood-evalctl scheduler decisions --from 2026-11-01T00:00Z --to 2026-11-02T00:00Z --job-id J-2345

Related playbooks and docs
--------------------------
- Probe asset lifecycle and retirement policy (see related_pages).
- Quant shadow cohort strategy and rollback guide.
- Annotator onboarding and labeling economy playbook.

Appendix: tuning knobs and recommended defaults
-----------------------------------------------
| knob | recommended default | rationale |
| daily_token_budget | 5_000_000 | medium-sized rollout for 1-2 models |
| cohort_weights | shadow:0.5,canary:0.2,prod_sample:0.3 | balance safety and coverage |
| priming_window | 30m to 2h | depends on model cold-start behavior |
| priming_hits | 8 | empirically reduces initial noise for kv-sensitive probes |
| snapshot_on_priming | true (private deployments) | speeds sidecar warm restarts |

If you have questions or want a runbook workshop for a specific model/tenant, contact Marina Kwon on Slack (#eval-playbook).
